list: The official 55 trophies, as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles before this guide was written (2026-11-18). Names, descriptions and grades are PlayStation's own words; the guides are ours.

sources.names: Exophase — grand-theft-auto-vi-psn/trophies — for every trophy's name, description and grade
sources.counts: PSNProfiles — trophies/43531-grand-theft-auto-vi — for the PSN list and the counts PlayStation tracks
sources.guides: Our own advice, built from the official description. Where a place or step is not pinned down by the description, the guide says so: it has not yet been checked in the game.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The platinum pops the moment the other 54 trophies are yours, so there is no separate task to chase. Treat it as the finish line of the roadmap below: story first, then the side strands and character finales, then activities and collectibles, then the money clean-up. Because the game had only just launched when this guide was written, treat any single number in a guide as a starting point and check it against the in-game tracker once you are playing.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Play the opening mission, Gone Fishing, to its end. It is the game's first story mission, so this is the first trophy most players will earn and it cannot be missed — just follow the story until the mission completes. If you are replaying the opening, the trophy is tied to finishing the mission, not to any optional objective inside it.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 1. Chapters complete in order, so keep playing the story and the trophy will pop at the chapter's final mission. There is no side content required: chapter trophies only count story progress, so you can leave collectibles and activities for later.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 2. Like the other chapter trophies it pops at the end of the chapter's last mission, so the only requirement is story progress. Use the time in Chapter 2 to start the easy side trophies — fishing, driving and the first activities — rather than rushing, since nothing in the chapter locks you out of them.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 3. The chapter trophy pops when the chapter's final mission ends. By this point the map is well opened up, so if you have been putting off the exploration trophy (The Goodtime State) or the vehicle-discovery count (Whip It Good), Chapter 3 is a good moment to start ticking them off between missions.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 4, the last numbered chapter. The trophy pops at the chapter's final mission and clears the way to the endgame. Before you push into the final mission, check the missables page: a few one-off trophies are easiest to attempt while story missions are still available, and the final stretch is the wrong time to discover you missed one.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: Complete the final story mission. It is the only gold trophy tied to the story, and it pops when the credits roll on the last mission — no optional objectives needed. Finish the missable trophies first if you can, because once the story is over the only way back to a missed story moment is a replay or an earlier save.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Breakfast Run. Mission trophies pop when the mission ends, so play it through and ignore any optional objectives unless you want them for yourself. If the mission is not on your map yet, keep following the story — named missions unlock in story order.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission The Cartel Heist. Heist missions in this game are story beats, so the trophy is a matter of reaching the mission in the story and finishing it. The heist is also a good moment to remember that the robbery trophies (Maximum Withdrawal, A Classic Blitz Play) are separate free-roam activities, not part of this mission.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Child's Play. As with the other named-mission trophies, the requirement is simply to finish the mission — there is no extra condition hidden in the description. If you want to be thorough, play the mission cleanly the first time: replays cost time, and the trophy only needs one completion.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Headliners. The name gives nothing away, so do not overthink it: reach the mission in the story and finish it. Headliners sits among the mid-story missions, so it will come to you in the normal flow of the chapters.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission VCIA Takedown. The VCIA airport shows up again in the free-roam trophy Catch Me If You Can, so while you are here for the story, note the layout: an unscheduled departure from the airport is a separate trophy you will want to attempt on your own terms later, not during this mission.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Operation Savage Glory. The operation-style name suggests a bigger set-piece mission, but the trophy itself asks for nothing more than a completion. Keep a save from before the mission if you like to replay set-pieces; the trophy does not need it, but the mission may be one you want to revisit.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Reach 100% completion in the game's own checklist. This is the long grind behind the platinum: it counts story missions, side strands, activities and collectibles, so it will fall naturally if you work the roadmap in order and finish the collectibles last. Check the in-game stats screen regularly — it is the only honest source for what percentage you are on, and this guide's counts are only as good as the official descriptions.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Pull off 250 stunts — jumps, near misses, airtime and the like — across free roam and missions. The count is cumulative, so the fastest way is to fold stunts into everything else you do: take jumps between objectives, drive fast through traffic, and use the stunt-friendly vehicles you find. Check the in-game stats for the running total rather than guessing, and do not leave all 250 for the endgame; they are a slow burn, not a sprint.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list and the 250-stunt count. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try every type of activity in the game at least once: racing, fishing, the shooting range, the arcade, bowling, meditation, hunting and the rest. You do not need to win or finish any of them — one attempt each is enough. This is the perfect first activity trophy: it maps the whole activity list for you, and every activity you sample here feeds a later, deeper trophy of its own.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in every Shooting Range challenge — 42 of them, according to the count PlayStation tracks. This is the game's hardest skill trophy: learn each challenge's target pattern, use the weapon the range gives you, and replay a challenge until the gold threshold is met. Work through the range early and in short sessions, because frustration builds fast on the later challenges; gold in all 42 is a matter of patience and repetition, not luck.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list and the 42-challenge count. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at every drone-race location in Leonida. Drone races are their own activity, so find each location on the map, enter the race, and win it — one win per location, not per race. Learn the course on a practice run first: drone handling is its own skill, and a clean line through the gates matters more than raw speed.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races. Different is the key word: the same race won twice counts once, so work through the race list and tick off new ones. Mix race types — street, off-road and whatever else the game offers — and pick a vehicle suited to each. If a race keeps beating you, come back with a better car or after more practice; there are more than 20 races available.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list and the 20-race count. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Cal is a named rival, so this is a head-to-head fishing contest rather than free fishing: find the challenge, take it on, and out-fish him. Fishing in this game is a timing activity — watch the line, keep the tension in the right zone, and reel steadily rather than yanking. If you lose, the challenge can be retried; the trophy only needs one win.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Complete any one arcade game. Find an arcade — the game's arcades host the classic cabinets — pick a game and play it to its end. Completion, not a high score, is what counts, so choose the shortest or easiest cabinet you can find. One completion is enough, and it also counts toward Master of None's activity sampler.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Andy's strand. Andy is one of the named contacts with a mission strand of their own: work through their missions in order until the strand ends. Strands unlock as the story progresses, so if Andy's missions are not showing yet, keep playing the main story and check back.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Kenton's strand. Like Andy's and Billy's, this is a side strand that runs beside the main story: finish Kenton's missions in order and the trophy pops at the last one. The boat in the name hints at where the strand goes, but the trophy itself only asks for the final mission's completion.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Billy's strand. Billy's missions are a side strand like Andy's and Kenton's: work through them in order until the last one is done. The rider in the name suggests bikes are involved, so keep a good bike handy when his missions come up — but the trophy only needs the final mission finished.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 stranger mission strands across Leonida. Strangers appear as markers on the map — meet them, take their missions, and see each strand through to its end. You need 8 complete strands, so do not stop after the first mission of each: a strand only counts when its last mission is done. Explore the whole state, because strangers are spread across it, not clustered in Vice City.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list and the 8-strand count. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Randy's strand. Randy is another named contact with a mission strand: finish their missions in order and the trophy pops at the last one. If the strand stalls, check whether a story chapter needs to finish first — side strands often gate on main-story progress.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Tyrone's strand. Tyrone's missions are a side strand like the others: work through them in order until the final mission is done. Keep an eye on the map for Tyrone's marker after each story chapter — new strand missions often appear when a chapter ends.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at every meditation spot in Leonida. Meditation spots are quiet places scattered across the state — find each one, sit down and meditate. The count is by spot, so one meditation per spot is enough. This pairs naturally with The Goodtime State's full exploration: visit the spots while you are touring the map anyway, and use the in-game map to track which ones you have found.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret. Bret is a stranger who wants one specific animal, not just any hunt: find the animal he names, track it, and take it down. Hunting rewards patience — move slowly, watch the wind and the animal's behaviour, and take the shot only when it is clean. If you spook it, back off and try again; the trophy needs the one animal Bret asked for.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Complete 3 full sets of collectible cards. Cards are hidden across Leonida, and a set only counts when every card in it is found — so this is really a scavenger hunt with three finish lines. Search thoroughly and tick each card off in this tracker as you find it; the cards are the kind of collectible that is easy to walk past and painful to hunt down one-by-one at the end.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list and the 3-set count. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: Use the WAiNK app — the game's in-world social app — at 100 different locations. This is a sightseeing trophy in disguise: travel the state, open WAiNK at each spot, and post. The count is by location, so revisit nothing twice. Pair it with exploration and meditation: every new place you visit is a WAiNK post waiting to happen, and 100 sounds like a lot until you realise how big Leonida is.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list and the 100-location count. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges. Challenges are the game's small objectives — the daily-style tasks and mini-goals scattered through activities and free roam. They stack up on their own if you play broadly, so do not chase them one by one: sample every activity, take the side objectives when they appear, and the count will climb. Check the in-game challenge list to see which ones you have already banked.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list and the 50-challenge count. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner beside you, build a 4-star wanted level, then lose the cops and escape. The partner is the catch: do it together, not solo. Rack up the heat in a quiet area with a fast car ready, then break line of sight, hide, and wait for the stars to fade. Plan your escape route before you start — a 4-star chase through busy streets ends badly, and a clean getaway needs open road and somewhere to hide.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: With your partner, rob 3 shops one after another without ever losing your wanted level — the trick is that the level must stay on the whole time. Plan a route past three shops, hit them in quick succession, and keep moving between them. Do not let the cops drop off between robberies: if the wanted level clears, the chain breaks and you start over. Fast car, short route, no dawdling.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles. Discovery means getting close enough for the game to register a new vehicle — driving past a parked car counts, so cruise every district and car park and the count climbs fast. The number sounds big, but Leonida is full of variety: cars, bikes, trucks, boats and more all count. This pairs with On the Spot's registration count and with general exploration.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list and the 100-vehicle count. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies during one single use of Combat Focus — the game's slow-down aiming mode. Find a fight with at least five enemies close together, trigger Combat Focus, and chain the kills before the meter runs out. Pick a crowded firefight rather than a quiet one: you need five targets in one window, so a mission with grouped enemies or a busy wanted-level shootout is the place to try it. If the meter ends at four, try again — the trophy needs five in one go.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list and the 5-enemy count. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure from VCIA — the Vice City airport. In plain terms: steal a plane and take off without filing a flight plan, or leave the airport in a way the tower did not schedule. Get onto the tarmac, grab an aircraft, and get airborne. Expect a wanted level the moment you do it, so have a plan for after take-off — or just enjoy the flight and deal with the heat later.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: The description is a joke with no instructions, so read it as a tank trophy: get into a Rhino tank and do what tanks do. Find a Rhino — military bases and the right wanted level are the usual sources — climb in, and cause enough mayhem for the game to credit you. The exact trigger is not pinned down by the description, so try the obvious first: drive it, fire it, and survive in it for a while. This one is flagged as worth checking in the game rather than trusting a guess.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected. Stealth is the whole requirement: plan the approach, get in and out without raising the alarm, and do not let a guard or camera spot you. Go in quiet, move slowly, and leave before anyone knows you were there. If you are spotted, the attempt fails — abort, lose the heat, and try again with a better route.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape after each one. Vaults are the big robberies: plan each hit, get in, take the money, and get out clean. Five separate vaults, five escapes — the count is cumulative, so you can space them out across the game. Bring a fast getaway car and know your exit before you go in; the escape is the part that fails most often, not the robbery itself.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list and the 5-vault count. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape. Armored trucks patrol the roads: intercept one, stop it, take the cash, and get away before the cops close in. The robbery is the easy half — the escape is what the trophy counts, so have a getaway vehicle ready and a route out of the area before you strike. One clean hit and escape is enough.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Explore every part of Leonida — the whole state, not just Vice City. Drive, fly and sail into every region until the map is filled in: the coast, the swamps, the small towns and the back roads. This is the trophy that makes all the other exploration trophies easier, because it forces you to visit the places where meditation spots, WAiNK locations and strangers are hiding. Do it in stages between story missions rather than as one long drive.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each gang in Leonida. Every gang runs operations somewhere in the state: find one per gang, hit it, and move on to the next gang's. You will need to know which gang holds which territory, so explore first and note the gang markers. The trophy counts gangs, not operations, so one hit per gang is enough.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Go to Ocean Beach, order a cocktail, and enjoy the view. This is a small moment trophy: find a bar or beach spot on Ocean Beach with a view, buy the cocktail, and the trophy should pop while you are sitting with it. It is easy to miss simply because it is so specific — you have to be at Ocean Beach, with a cocktail, looking at the view — so make a deliberate trip rather than hoping to stumble into it.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Drive a vehicle straight through a showroom window and out the other side — the classic getaway. Find a vehicle showroom, get a car inside or line one up at the glass, and smash your way out. The trophy wants the style as much as the act: a clean, fast exit through the frontage, not a slow scrape. Expect damage and a wanted level, so pick your showroom and your exit route first.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Visit the Kolt & Associates bowling alley and bowl — follow through on the shot. This is the bowling alley's own trophy: go to the alley, pick up a ball, and bowl a full game or at least a proper follow-through. It is a small, specific moment, so make a deliberate trip to the alley rather than hoping to stumble into it. It pairs with Ten Pin, the bowling alley's other trophy.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: The description is deliberately vague — a partnership with mass appeal — so this one is about your partnership with your co-lead reaching a wide audience. The most likely reading is a story or side moment where the two of you go public together, so play the story and the partner strands and watch for a moment built around the pair. The exact trigger is not pinned down by the description, so treat this as one to check in the game rather than to force.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: Make a choice — for better or worse. This is a story-choice trophy: at some point the game offers a decision, and this pops when you make it. The description gives no hint which choice, so the honest advice is to play the story and decide as you go; the trophy will come when a real choice arrives. Keep a save from before big decisions if you like to see both outcomes — the trophy only needs one choice made.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: Second time's the charm — this pops when something works on the second attempt. The most likely reading is a retry: fail a specific attempt once, then succeed on the second try. Which attempt is not pinned down by the description, so do not force it: play normally, and if a mission or activity fails once and you clear it on the retry, watch for the pop. It is flagged missable because a first-time success may not count.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: What the hell just happened? — this is the game's surprise trophy, earned by stumbling into something strange. Expect an odd event, a weird encounter or an unexpected scene somewhere in Leonida: the kind of moment you cannot plan for and can only find by exploring and paying attention. Wander the odd corners of the map, follow strange markers, and talk to stranger characters — the trophy will find you when you find the event.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Bowl someone over with a melee drive-by — a melee attack from a moving vehicle. The bowling alley's other trophy suggests the setting: drive past a target at the alley and hit them with a melee weapon from the vehicle. Line up the pass, time the swing, and keep moving. It is a one-shot setup, so practice the approach on a quiet road first if you keep missing, then take it to the alley.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Launder $250,000 of Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills are dirty money from robberies and heists: take them to a contact who can clean them, and the laundered total counts toward the $250,000. It is cumulative, so every robbery feeds it — keep laundering as you go rather than saving it all for the end. If your contacts are not offering laundering yet, keep playing the story until the option opens.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops in the game. The count is cumulative and across every shop type — clothes, weapons, cars, food and more — so just buy what you need as you play and the total will climb. Late in the game, if you are short, the fastest top-up is an expensive vehicle or weapon. Keep an eye on the total in the in-game stats and do not hoard cash for no reason.
trophies.sources: Exophase — name, description, grade. PSNProfiles — the PSN list and the $100,000 count. Our own advice from the official description; not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Buy every garage property in the game. Garages are properties you can purchase — find each one for sale, pay for it, and the trophy pops when the last one is yours. You will need serious money, so this is a late-game purchase: save it for after the big heists, or buy garages one by one as your cash allows. Check the property listings regularly so you do not miss a garage tucked away in a quieter district.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. The app is the game's vehicle service — open it, register a vehicle you own or have found, and repeat until 10 are on the books. The count is cumulative, so register every new vehicle as you find it rather than saving them up. It pairs naturally with Whip It Good's 100-vehicle discovery: every vehicle you discover is a candidate for registration.
